title: Bhishma's terrible vow
hookLine: the Kaurava commander loves the men he is fighting, and the reason he's there at all is a vow he made as a young prince.
carry: bhishma pratigya: a vow that binds for life

lines: HIS TERMS: NOT THE FIVE BROTHERS
cards: An army might want a commander who hates the enemy. Duryodhana's commander doesn't. When Duryodhana asked Bhishma to lead his forces, in the Udyoga book, the old man said yes, and then set terms.
The sons of Pandu, he said, are as dear to me as you are. I will fight their armies for you. I will not kill them.
And there was a second problem, standing right there in the hall: Karna. Today, Bhishma's fall begins, with the strange shape of the side he leads.

teach.h: KARNA WON'T FIGHT WHILE BHISHMA LIVES
teach.b: Start with Karna. When Bhishma ranks the warriors on his own side, he rates Karna low, and Karna is stung. So Karna makes a vow of his own: as long as Bhishma lives, he will not fight.
Now go back to his youth.
Bhishma was born Devavrata, a prince and heir to the throne.

teach.h: THE BOON: DEATH WHEN HE CHOOSES
teach.b: When his father, King Shantanu, fell in love with Satyavati, her father wanted her sons to rule. So the young prince gave up the throne, and then, so that no child of his could ever claim it, swore never to marry.
The epic says flowers rained from the sky, and he was called Bhishma: the one of the terrible vow. His father gave him a gift in return: death would not take him until he chose it.
That vow is why he's here, bound to the throne he gave away, leading an army against grandsons he loves. In Hindi, an unbreakable promise is still called a Bhishma pratigya, a vow like Bhishma's.
Hindus prize a vow kept, and many keep vows of their own, vrats of fasting or prayer on certain days. But the epic doesn't make it simple.

Many readers see Bhishma's vow as both his greatness and his tragedy: a promise made out of love that now binds him to the wrong side. On the first day, Virata's sons Uttara and Shveta fall, Shveta at Bhishma's own hand.
So how do you bring down a man who can't be beaten, and who chooses when he dies?

how: Bhishma's vow and the boon that lets him choose his death are told in the Mahabharata's Adi book, and 'Bhishma pratigya' is still used in Hindi for an unbreakable vow.

o: the day the grandsire first takes command of the army
the moment Karna finally joins the battle against Arjuna
the grandsire's slow end: he can't be beaten, and picks his hour

games.q: who's who on the Kaurava side? tap the pairs.
p: commands, but won't kill the five
gave him death when he chose

s: Bhishma agreed to kill the Pandava brothers when he took command
he said they were as dear to him as Duryodhana; he'd fight their armies, not kill them.
Karna vowed not to fight as long as Bhishma lived
stung at being ranked low, he stayed out until Bhishma fell.
'Bhishma' was the name he was given at birth
he was born Devavrata; he was called Bhishma, the one of the terrible vow, after he swore it.

games.q: you're young Prince Devavrata. your father loves Satyavati, but her father wants her sons to rule, not yours. what do you do?
o: tell your father to forget her: you're the heir.
give up the throne, and swear never to marry.
wait until you're king, then decide.
games.why: he gave up the throne, then swore never to marry. flowers rained down, and he was called Bhishma, the one of the terrible vow.

practice: Many Hindus keep a vrat, a vow of fasting or prayer, on certain days. Think of a promise you carry: to a person, a practice, a family role. Breathing in, feel its weight honestly.

Breathing out, ask yourself quietly whether it still serves what's good, the question Bhishma's story leaves us with. If you pray, bring that promise into your prayer. If you don't, simply hold it up to the light.

wordCard.voice: Bhishma's fall. Not yet. Today it's a riddle: a commander bound by his own vow, who will die only when he chooses.

orig.note: Bhishma, 'the terrible': the name he earned by his vow; he was born Devavrata.

carryVoice: Your line: bhishma pratigya: a vow that binds for life. The riddle is set, and the answer will take days. Day eight hundred twenty-five, done.
